subject: B
topic: First in World & India (Adventure, Sports, Discoveries)

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Who was the first person to reach the summit of Mount Everest?
questions.explanation: Edmund Hillary (New Zealand) and Tenzing Norgay (Nepal/India) became the first persons to summit Mount Everest on 29 May 1953. George Mallory and Andrew Irvine is wrong — they attempted in 1924 but disappeared near the summit; their success was never confirmed. Reinhold Messner and Peter Habeler is wrong — they were the first to climb Everest without supplemental oxygen (1978). Jim Whittaker and Nawang Gombu is wrong — Whittaker was the first American to summit (1963).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about 'firsts' in Indian sports:

(i) Major Dhyan Chand is known as the wizard of hockey.
(ii) India won its first Olympic gold medal in hockey at the 1928 Amsterdam Olympics.
(iii) Abhinav Bindra won India's first individual Olympic gold medal in 2008.
(iv) India's first Cricket World Cup victory was in 1987.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Major Dhyan Chand is famously called the 'Wizard of Hockey' for his extraordinary skills. (ii) is correct — India won its first Olympic gold in field hockey at the 1928 Amsterdam Olympics. (iii) is correct — Abhinav Bindra won the 10m Air Rifle gold at the 2008 Beijing Olympics, India's first individual Olympic gold. (iv) is wrong — India won its first Cricket World Cup in 1983 under Kapil Dev's captaincy, not 1987.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Who was the first woman to travel in space?
questions.explanation: Valentina Tereshkova (Soviet Union) became the first woman in space on 16 June 1963 aboard Vostok 6. Sally Ride is wrong — she was the first American woman in space (1983). Kalpana Chawla is wrong — she was the first Indian-American woman in space (1997). Svetlana Savitskaya is wrong — she was the second woman in space (1982) and first woman to perform a spacewalk.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Yuri Gagarin is regarded as the first human to journey into outer space.
Reason (R): Gagarin orbited the Earth aboard Vostok 1 on 12 April 1961.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — Yuri Gagarin (Soviet Union) was the first human in space. Reason (R) is also correct — he completed one orbit of Earth aboard Vostok 1 on 12 April 1961. (R) explains (A) because it provides the specific mission details that made him the first human in space. Option 2 is wrong because (R) is the factual basis for (A). Option 3 is wrong because (R) is historically accurate. Option 4 is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following 'firsts' with the correct persons:

Column I:
(a) First man on the Moon
(b) First person to reach the South Pole
(c) First person to swim across the English Channel
(d) First person to sail around the world

Column II:
(i) Ferdinand Magellan (expedition)
(ii) Neil Armstrong
(iii) Captain Matthew Webb
(iv) Roald Amundsen

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a) Neil Armstrong was the first man on the Moon (20 July 1969) — matches (ii). (b) Roald Amundsen (Norway) reached the South Pole first on 14 December 1911 — matches (iv). (c) Captain Matthew Webb was the first to swim the English Channel in 1875 — matches (iii). (d) Ferdinand Magellan's expedition (completed by Juan Sebastián Elcano) was the first to circumnavigate the globe (1519–1522) — matches (i). Option 2 swaps South Pole and Channel. Option 3 swaps Moon and South Pole. Option 4 swaps Channel and circumnavigation.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are correct 'firsts' for India?

(i) First satellite launched by India — Aryabhata (1975)
(ii) First Indian in space — Rakesh Sharma (1984)
(iii) First woman President of India — Pratibha Patil (2007)
(iv) First Indian to win a Nobel Prize — Rabindranath Tagore (1913)

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Aryabhata was India's first satellite, launched on 19 April 1975 by a Soviet rocket. (ii) is correct — Squadron Leader Rakesh Sharma became the first Indian in space on 3 April 1984 aboard Soyuz T-11. (iii) is correct — Pratibha Patil was India's first woman President (2007–2012). (iv) is correct — Rabindranath Tagore won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913 for 'Gitanjali'. All four are correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The first successful heart transplant in the world was performed by:
questions.explanation: Dr. Christiaan Barnard performed the world's first successful human heart transplant on 3 December 1967 at Groote Schuur Hospital, Cape Town, South Africa. Dr. Michael DeBakey is wrong — he was a pioneer in cardiovascular surgery but did not perform the first heart transplant. Dr. Denton Cooley is wrong — he performed the first artificial heart implant (1969), not the first transplant. Dr. William Harvey is wrong — he discovered blood circulation in 1628, centuries before transplant surgery.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about 'firsts' in world discoveries:

(i) Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin in 1928.
(ii) Isaac Newton discovered the law of gravitation.
(iii) Marie Curie discovered the telephone.
(iv) Edward Jenner developed the first successful vaccine (smallpox).

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin (the first antibiotic) in 1928 at St. Mary's Hospital, London. (ii) is correct — Isaac Newton formulated the law of universal gravitation. (iv) is correct — Edward Jenner developed the first successful vaccine against smallpox in 1796. (iii) is wrong — Marie Curie discovered radium and polonium; the telephone was invented by Alexander Graham Bell in 1876.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The first Indian woman to climb Mount Everest was __________.
questions.explanation: Bachendri Pal became the first Indian woman to summit Mount Everest on 23 May 1984. Arunima Sinha is wrong — she was the first female amputee to climb Everest (2013). Santosh Yadav is wrong — she was the first woman to climb Everest twice (1992, 1993), but Bachendri Pal was the first Indian woman. Malavath Purna is wrong — she was one of the youngest Indians to climb Everest (2014).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Who was the first person to reach the North Pole?
questions.explanation: Robert Peary (USA) is traditionally credited as the first to reach the North Pole on 6 April 1909 (though disputed). Roald Amundsen is wrong — he was the first to reach the South Pole (1911) and first verified to fly over the North Pole (1926). Ernest Shackleton is wrong — he is famous for Antarctic expeditions but never reached either Pole. James Cook is wrong — he was an 18th-century explorer of the Pacific, not a polar explorer.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): India is the first country to reach the south polar region of the Moon.
Reason (R): ISRO's Chandrayaan-3 successfully landed near the lunar south pole on 23 August 2023.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — India became the first country to land a spacecraft near the Moon's south pole. Reason (R) is also correct — Chandrayaan-3's Vikram lander successfully soft-landed on 23 August 2023. (R) explains (A) because this specific mission achievement is what made India the first to reach the lunar south polar region. Option 2 is wrong because (R) directly explains (A). Option 3 is wrong because (R) is factually accurate. Option 4 is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following Indian 'firsts' with the correct persons:

Column I:
(a) First Indian to win an Olympic individual gold
(b) First Indian woman to win an Olympic medal
(c) First Indian to win a Grand Slam tennis title
(d) First Indian chess Grandmaster

Column II:
(i) Viswanathan Anand
(ii) Abhinav Bindra
(iii) Karnam Malleswari
(iv) Leander Paes (doubles)

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a) Abhinav Bindra won India's first individual Olympic gold (2008, shooting) — matches (ii). (b) Karnam Malleswari was the first Indian woman to win an Olympic medal (bronze, weightlifting, 2000 Sydney) — matches (iii). (c) Leander Paes won a Grand Slam doubles title (1999 Wimbledon doubles with Mahesh Bhupathi) — matches (iv). (d) Viswanathan Anand became India's first chess Grandmaster in 1988 — matches (i). Option 2 swaps (a) and (b). Option 3 swaps (b) and (c). Option 4 swaps (c) and (d).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The first newspaper published in India was:
questions.explanation: The Bengal Gazette (also called Hickey's Gazette) was the first newspaper printed in India, started by James Augustus Hickey in January 1780 in Calcutta. The Hindu is wrong — it was founded much later in 1878. Times of India is wrong — it was established in 1838 as The Bombay Times. Bombay Samachar is wrong — though it's the oldest existing newspaper in Asia (1822), it was not the first newspaper in India.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are correctly matched 'firsts' in world sports?

(i) First modern Olympic Games — Athens, 1896
(ii) First FIFA World Cup — Uruguay, 1930
(iii) First T20 Cricket World Cup — South Africa, 2007
(iv) First Paralympic Games — London, 1948

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — the first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens, Greece in 1896. (ii) is correct — the first FIFA World Cup was held in Uruguay in 1930, won by the host nation. (iii) is correct — the first ICC T20 World Cup was held in South Africa in 2007, won by India. (iv) is correct — the first Paralympic Games (then called Stoke Mandeville Games for disabled veterans) were held in London in 1948. All four are correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic Ocean was:
questions.explanation: Amelia Earhart became the first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic Ocean on 20 May 1932. Bessie Coleman is wrong — she was the first African-American woman and Native American to hold a pilot's licence (1921). Harriet Quimby is wrong — she was the first woman to fly across the English Channel (1912). Jacqueline Cochran is wrong — she was the first woman to break the sound barrier (1953).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about 'firsts' in Indian science and technology:

(i) India's first nuclear test (Smiling Buddha) was conducted in 1974.
(ii) India's first supercomputer was PARAM 8000.
(iii) Homi J. Bhabha is known as the father of India's nuclear programme.
(iv) India's first space mission was Chandrayaan-1.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — India's first nuclear test 'Smiling Buddha' (Pokhran-I) was conducted on 18 May 1974. (ii) is correct — PARAM 8000, developed by C-DAC in 1991, was India's first supercomputer. (iii) is correct — Homi J. Bhabha founded the Atomic Energy Commission and is called the father of India's nuclear programme. (iv) is wrong — India's first space mission was not Chandrayaan-1 (2008); India's space programme began with sounding rockets in 1963, and the first satellite was Aryabhata (1975).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Wright Brothers are credited with inventing the first successful airplane.
Reason (R): Orville and Wilbur Wright made the first powered, sustained, and controlled airplane flight at Kitty Hawk on 17 December 1903.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — the Wright Brothers are credited with inventing the first successful airplane. Reason (R) is also correct — their flight at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina on 17 December 1903 lasted 12 seconds covering 36 metres. (R) explains (A) because this specific achievement (powered, sustained, controlled flight) is what established them as the inventors of the airplane. Option 2 is wrong because (R) provides the evidence for (A). Option 3 is wrong because (R) is historically accurate. Option 4 is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The first Indian to receive the Nobel Prize in Physics was __________.
questions.explanation: Sir C.V. Raman won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1930 for his discovery of the Raman Effect (scattering of light). Hargobind Khorana is wrong — he won the Nobel Prize in Physiology/Medicine (1968), not Physics. S. Chandrasekhar is wrong — while he won the Nobel in Physics (1983), he was a naturalised American citizen, and C.V. Raman preceded him. Amartya Sen is wrong — he won the Nobel Prize in Economics (1998), not Physics.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The first Test cricket match in history was played between:
questions.explanation: The first Test cricket match was played between Australia and England at the Melbourne Cricket Ground from 15–19 March 1877. India and England is wrong — India played its first Test in 1932. Australia and South Africa is wrong — South Africa's first Test was in 1889. England and West Indies is wrong — West Indies' first Test was in 1928.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following world 'firsts' with their year:

Column I:
(a) First television broadcast
(b) First email sent
(c) First mobile phone call
(d) First website created

Column II:
(i) 1991
(ii) 1973
(iii) 1927
(iv) 1971

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a) First television demonstration by Philo Farnsworth / John Logie Baird in 1927 — matches (iii). (b) First email was sent by Ray Tomlinson in 1971 — matches (iv). (c) First mobile phone call was made by Martin Cooper (Motorola) in 1973 — matches (ii). (d) First website was created by Tim Berners-Lee at CERN in 1991 — matches (i). Option 2 swaps (a) and (b). Option 3 swaps (c) and (d). Option 4 swaps (b) and (c).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Who was the first Indian woman to go into space?
questions.explanation: Kalpana Chawla became the first Indian-born woman in space when she flew aboard Space Shuttle Columbia (STS-87) on 19 November 1997. Sunita Williams is wrong — she went to space in 2006, after Kalpana Chawla. Sirisha Bandla is wrong — she flew to space in 2021 on Virgin Galactic. Shawna Pandya is wrong — she is an astronaut candidate but has not been to space.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about 'firsts' in adventure:

(i) Jacques Piccard and Don Walsh were the first to reach the deepest point of the ocean (Mariana Trench) in 1960.
(ii) Sir Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay were the first to summit K2.
(iii) Roald Amundsen was the first to reach the South Pole in 1911.
(iv) Charles Lindbergh was the first to fly solo non-stop across the Atlantic in 1927.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Jacques Piccard and Don Walsh descended to the Challenger Deep in the bathyscaphe Trieste on 23 January 1960. (iii) is correct — Roald Amundsen reached the South Pole on 14 December 1911. (iv) is correct — Charles Lindbergh flew solo non-stop across the Atlantic on 20–21 May 1927 in the Spirit of St. Louis. (ii) is wrong — Hillary and Tenzing summited Mount Everest, not K2; K2 was first climbed by Achille Compagnoni and Lino Lacedelli in 1954.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The first Indian to win the Miss World title was:
questions.explanation: Reita Faria became the first Indian (and first Asian) to win the Miss World title in 1966. Aishwarya Rai is wrong — she won Miss World in 1994. Sushmita Sen is wrong — she won Miss Universe (not Miss World) in 1994. Diana Hayden is wrong — she won Miss World in 1997.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Alexander Graham Bell is credited with inventing the telephone.
Reason (R): Bell received the first US patent for the telephone on 7 March 1876.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — Alexander Graham Bell is widely credited as the inventor of the first practical telephone. Reason (R) is also correct — Bell was granted US Patent No. 174,465 on 7 March 1876 for the telephone. (R) explains (A) because the patent legally established Bell as the inventor. Option 2 is wrong because the patent is the formal recognition that supports (A). Option 3 is wrong because (R) is historically documented. Option 4 is wrong because (A) is the accepted historical view.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are correct Indian 'firsts' in sports?

(i) Sachin Tendulkar — first cricketer to score 100 international centuries
(ii) P.T. Usha — first Indian woman to reach an Olympic final in athletics
(iii) Milkha Singh — first Indian to win an Olympic gold in athletics
(iv) Neeraj Chopra — first Indian to win an Olympic gold in athletics (javelin)

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Sachin Tendulkar scored 100 centuries in international cricket, an unmatched record. (ii) is correct — P.T. Usha reached the 400m hurdles final at the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics, missing bronze by 1/100th of a second. (iv) is correct — Neeraj Chopra won Olympic gold in javelin throw at the 2020 Tokyo Olympics (held 2021), making him the first Indian to win an Olympic gold in athletics. (iii) is wrong — Milkha Singh narrowly missed an Olympic medal (4th in 400m, 1960 Rome); he never won an Olympic gold.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The first country to grant women the right to vote was:
questions.explanation: New Zealand became the first self-governing country to grant all women the right to vote in 1893. United States is wrong — women gained the right to vote nationally in 1920 (19th Amendment). United Kingdom is wrong — women over 30 gained voting rights in 1918, full equality in 1928. France is wrong — French women gained voting rights in 1944.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following discoveries with their discoverers:

Column I:
(a) X-rays
(b) Radioactivity
(c) Electron
(d) Blood circulation

Column II:
(i) William Harvey
(ii) Wilhelm Roentgen
(iii) Henri Becquerel
(iv) J.J. Thomson

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a) X-rays were discovered by Wilhelm Roentgen in 1895 — matches (ii). (b) Radioactivity was discovered by Henri Becquerel in 1896 — matches (iii). (c) The electron was discovered by J.J. Thomson in 1897 — matches (iv). (d) Blood circulation was described by William Harvey in 1628 — matches (i). Option 2 swaps X-rays and Radioactivity. Option 3 swaps Radioactivity and Electron. Option 4 swaps Electron and Blood circulation.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The first Indian railway train ran on 16 April 1853 between which stations?
questions.explanation: The first passenger train in India ran on 16 April 1853 from Bori Bunder (now Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus) in Bombay to Thane, a distance of 34 km. Calcutta and Delhi is wrong — that route was built much later. Madras and Bangalore is wrong — the Madras Railway came later. Bombay and Pune is wrong — while the Great Indian Peninsula Railway later extended to Pune, the first run was only to Thane.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about 'firsts' in world history:

(i) The first country to use paper currency was China.
(ii) The first university in the world was the University of Oxford.
(iii) The first country to reach Mars was the United States.
(iv) The first printed book was the Gutenberg Bible (1455).

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — China introduced paper currency during the Tang Dynasty (7th century AD), formalized in the Song Dynasty. (iii) is correct — NASA's Mariner 4 was the first spacecraft to successfully fly by Mars (1965), and Viking 1 was the first to land (1976). (iv) is correct — the Gutenberg Bible, printed by Johannes Gutenberg around 1455, is considered the first major book printed using movable type. (ii) is wrong — the University of Bologna (1088) and University of Al-Qarawiyyin (859 AD) are older than Oxford.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The first Indian woman to receive the Bharat Ratna was:
questions.explanation: Indira Gandhi was the first Indian woman to receive the Bharat Ratna, awarded posthumously in 1971. Wait — actually Indira Gandhi received it in 1971 while alive. Let me correct: Indira Gandhi received the Bharat Ratna in 1971, making her the first woman to receive this honour. Mother Teresa is wrong — she received it in 1980. Sarojini Naidu is wrong — she never received the Bharat Ratna. M.S. Subbulakshmi is wrong — she received it in 1998.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Who invented the World Wide Web (WWW)?
questions.explanation: Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web in 1989 while working at CERN, making information sharing via hyperlinks possible. Vint Cerf is wrong — he is known as a 'father of the Internet' for developing TCP/IP protocols, not the Web specifically. Bill Gates is wrong — he co-founded Microsoft but did not invent the Web. Steve Jobs is wrong — he co-founded Apple but did not invent the Web.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about Indian firsts in technology:

(i) India's first Mars mission (Mangalyaan/MOM) was launched in 2013.
(ii) India became the first Asian country to reach Mars orbit on its first attempt.
(iii) ISRO was established in 1969.
(iv) India's first indigenous aircraft carrier is INS Vikrant.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Mangalyaan (Mars Orbiter Mission) was launched on 5 November 2013 and entered Mars orbit on 24 September 2014. (ii) is correct — India became the first Asian nation and first in the world to reach Mars orbit on its maiden attempt. (iii) is correct — ISRO (Indian Space Research Organisation) was established on 15 August 1969. (iv) is correct — INS Vikrant (commissioned 2022) is India's first indigenously built aircraft carrier. All four are correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The first woman to serve as Prime Minister of any country was:
questions.explanation: Sirimavo Bandaranaike of Sri Lanka (then Ceylon) became the world's first female Prime Minister in 1960. Indira Gandhi is wrong — she became PM of India in 1966, six years after Bandaranaike. Golda Meir is wrong — she became PM of Israel in 1969. Margaret Thatcher is wrong — she became PM of the UK in 1979.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are correctly matched Indian 'firsts'?

(i) First Indian airline — Tata Airlines (1932)
(ii) First Indian film — Raja Harishchandra (1913)
(iii) First Indian bank — Reserve Bank of India (1935)
(iv) First Indian university — University of Calcutta (1857)

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Tata Airlines (later Air India) was India's first airline, started in 1932 by J.R.D. Tata. (ii) is correct — Raja Harishchandra (1913), directed by Dadasaheb Phalke, was the first full-length Indian feature film. (iv) is correct — the University of Calcutta (along with Bombay and Madras) was established in 1857, among the first modern universities in India. (iii) is wrong — RBI (1935) is the central bank, not the first commercial bank; the first Indian bank was the Bank of Hindustan (1770) or Allahabad Bank (1865) among Indian-managed banks.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The first human to perform a spacewalk (EVA) was:
questions.explanation: Alexei Leonov (Soviet Union) performed the first-ever spacewalk (Extra-Vehicular Activity) on 18 March 1965 during the Voskhod 2 mission. Edward White is wrong — he was the first American to spacewalk (June 1965), but Leonov preceded him by three months. Neil Armstrong is wrong — he is famous for being the first on the Moon, not the first spacewalker. Buzz Aldrin is wrong — he walked on the Moon but was not the first spacewalker.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Dadasaheb Phalke is called the father of Indian cinema.
Reason (R): He directed 'Raja Harishchandra' in 1913, which was the first full-length Indian feature film.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — Dadasaheb Phalke (Dhundiraj Govind Phalke) is known as the father of Indian cinema. Reason (R) is also correct — he directed Raja Harishchandra (1913), India's first full-length feature film. (R) explains (A) because this pioneering achievement in filmmaking is the primary reason he is called the father of Indian cinema. Option 2 is wrong because (R) provides the exact reason for (A). Option 3 is wrong because (R) is historically accurate. Option 4 is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The first Indian to receive the Nobel Prize in Economics was:
questions.explanation: Amartya Sen won the Nobel Prize in Economics (officially the Sveriges Riksbank Prize) in 1998 for his contributions to welfare economics and social choice theory. Abhijit Banerjee is wrong — he won the Nobel in Economics in 2019 (later than Sen), and is of Indian origin but holds American citizenship. Jagdish Bhagwati is wrong — he is a renowned economist but has not won the Nobel Prize. Manmohan Singh is wrong — he was India's PM and an economist but has not won the Nobel Prize.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The first cloned animal in the world was:
questions.explanation: Dolly the sheep was the first mammal to be cloned from an adult somatic cell, born on 5 July 1996 at the Roslin Institute, Scotland. Copy Cat is wrong — it was the first cloned cat (2001). Snuppy is wrong — it was the first cloned dog (2005). Idaho Gem is wrong — it was the first cloned equid/mule (2003). All came after Dolly.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following Indian 'firsts' with the correct year:

Column I:
(a) First general elections in India
(b) First nuclear test (Pokhran-I)
(c) First satellite (Aryabhata) launched
(d) First Asian Games hosted by India

Column II:
(i) 1975
(ii) 1951
(iii) 1974
(iv) 1951

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a) India's first general elections were held in 1951-52 — matches (ii). (b) India's first nuclear test (Pokhran-I / Smiling Buddha) was in 1974 — matches (iii). (c) Aryabhata satellite was launched in 1975 — matches (i). (d) India hosted the first Asian Games in New Delhi in 1951 — matches (iv). Option 2 swaps (a) and (b). Option 3 swaps (b) and (c). Option 4 swaps (c) and (d).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The first person to discover the sea route to India was:
questions.explanation: Vasco da Gama (Portugal) discovered the sea route to India, arriving at Calicut (Kozhikode) on 20 May 1498. Christopher Columbus is wrong — he discovered the Americas (1492) while trying to reach India. Bartholomew Dias is wrong — he rounded the Cape of Good Hope (1488) but did not reach India. Marco Polo is wrong — he travelled to India and China by land/sea earlier (13th century) but did not discover a new European sea route.
